intro.text: This entry describes an autosomal dominant form of nonsyndromic hearing loss designated DFNA55. I do not reliably recall the causal gene or the primary reports for this locus, so they are not given here.

checks.claim: DFNA55 is an autosomal dominant form of nonsyndromic hearing loss.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper is a study of Tectb knockout mice (cochlear tuning, tectorial membrane structure). It never mentions DFNA55, autosomal dominant inheritance or human nonsyndromic hearing loss.

paragraphs.text: DFNA55 is a form of autosomal dominant nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss. Its specific clinical course, the gene involved and the reports that define it could not be confirmed from memory, so they are left out.

checks.claim: DFNA55 is a form of autosomal dominant nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not mention DFNA55 or describe any human hearing-loss phenotype. It only reports a low-frequency hearing loss in Tectb-/- mice.

paragraphs.text: As its designation shows, DFNA55 is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.

checks.claim: DFNA55 is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not address DFNA55 or its inheritance pattern. The mouse phenotype it describes is in homozygous (Tectb-/-) mice, not dominant.
